I am incredibly particular about my nails, so when I say this salon impressed me, I mean it genuinely.

The level of attention to detail was evident. Without me having to ask, they applied two coats of base and three coats of colour as a matter of course, exactly the way it should be done, and exactly the kind of thing that separates a truly skilled nail technician from an average one. The design I brought as a reference was replicated with impressive accuracy, and the range of colours available made the whole selection process an absolute joy.

Shaping is usually where I am very particular of. I have almond-shaped nails and getting that right on the first try is not something many salons can do, but they did, effortlessly and without a single correction needed. For my pedicure, they used a fine brush to bring the polish right to the very edge of each nail, a technique reminiscent of a Russian manicure, and the finish was immaculate.

The salon itself is clean, well-spaced, and comfortable, with two dedicated technicians, one for manicure, one for pedicure, so everything flows efficiently without feeling rushed.

For context on value: nail design, gel removal, chrome, pedicure gel and removal came to 750,000 VND in total. Exceptional quality at an exceptional price.

Yes, they did ask me to leave a review, but I want to be clear that I would have written this regardless, because results like these deserve to be shared. I will absolutely be back the next time I’m in Da Nang.

Extremely disappointed! Great tips and trust in return for sloppy work and excuses
I just got a cat-eye manicure at this shop yesterday (costing 300,000 VND). I thought the service was good back then and even went out of my way to exchange money to give the nail artist a tip. Trusting them, I came back today to get a pedicure, also paying 300,000 VND. However, I was met with completely unreasonable double standards and treatment:
1. Excuses and Inconsistent Standards: The nail tech first excused herself by saying my toenails were too small for cat-eye style and I could only get a regular solid color. But yesterday when doing my fingers, they explicitly said they could mix colors and do cat-eye. Today, they refused any color blending, showing completely inconsistent standards.
2. Severe Drop in Quality and Time: Yesterday’s manicure took 50 minutes, while today’s pedicure was rushed and finished in just 25 minutes. The final result looks like cheap, ordinary nail polish—completely incomparable to a proper cat-eye effect.
3. Heartless and Defensive Attitude: When I raised the issue with the shop, they rudely brushed it off by saying "pedicures naturally take less time," completely dodging the core problem: charging the price of a cat-eye while only providing a cheap single-color polish without any mention of a refund!
We treat the shop with kindness, trust, and tips, only to be met with sloppy, low-quality service and a defensive attitude. It is completely unacceptable! I have retracted my 5-star review from yesterday and posted this honest review to expose their true colors—"nice on the first visit, dismissive on the second." I will definitely never come back again!

reviewList.text:
We booked the 90-minute four-hands massage hoping for a relaxing and rejuvenating experience. We get massages regularly both in the US and while traveling, and have experienced four-hands treatments in many countries, so we have a solid basis for comparison.

While the massage may be acceptable by local standards, it did not feel like a true four-hands experience. The therapists were not synchronized at all. At one point, my left hand and fingers were being pulled while nothing was happening on the right side, which completely disrupted the flow a four-hands massage is meant to provide.

Communication was also very challenging. Without using a translation app, it was nearly impossible to communicate with the therapists. When I asked them to skip the bottoms of my feet, they didn’t understand. When I requested lighter pressure, they simply stopped working on that area altogether. During the session, my husband’s therapists chatted and giggled for much of the time, and my younger therapist occasionally joined in, while the older therapist remained mostly quiet. This was distracting and not relaxing—people go to spas to unwind, not to listen to staff conversations.

We had four therapists in total. The older therapist appeared to be guiding the other three, but one of the younger therapists pulled my left arm so forcefully that it caused pain, and I had to ask them to stop. The therapists also took bathroom breaks during the session. What made this uncomfortable was that they were using the bathroom inside the room, as we repeatedly heard toilet flushing, which felt unprofessional. One therapist slipped a couple of times while applying oil to my shoulder, indicating excessive oil use and poorly controlled movements. My left arm was still sore 48 hours later.

We didn't need pickup services and received the complimentary shampoo service while my husband had the foot scrub. I was led into a dimly lit room where three men were already having their hair washed, which was extremely uncomfortable. I later met them at check out and the guys also felt awkward when a stranger entered their space. I felt uneasy throughout the experience, unsure of what to expect. The stylist ended my session early, explaining that there were men in the room and took me back to the first floor to finish blow-drying my hair. For future guests, it would be helpful to clearly inform customers in advance that the shampoo area is a shared space so they can decide whether they are comfortable with that arrangement. My husband’s foot scrub, however, was fine. They also offer 15% discount off and I got a simply wax. Again, I used the translation app and it was ok.

Overall, the professionalism and coordination fell short of expectations. It wasn’t a terrible massage, but it was underwhelming and did not deliver the quality we anticipated. This service may be acceptable for guests new to four-hands massages, but for more experienced spa-goers, it may not meet expectations.

If you’re in Da Nang, Vietnam, do yourself a favor and book an appointment at EIRA Nails!

I had builder gel done on both my fingernails and toes, and y’all…I am beyond impressed. I’ve had my nails done all over the U.S., and I experienced techniques here that I’d never seen before. I found myself thinking, “Now where has THIS been all my life?”

What made this experience so special wasn’t just the beautiful results—it was the care. They paid attention to every tiny detail, never rushed, and treated me with such kindness from beginning to end. It felt less like a nail appointment and more like being pampered by people who genuinely take pride in their craft.

My nails are absolutely gorgeous, but honestly, the experience was just as beautiful. In a world where so many businesses are trying to get you in and out as quickly as possible, EIRA Nails reminded me what true customer care feels like.

Da Nang has won my heart, and EIRA Nails is one of the reasons why. If you want meticulous work, exceptional service, and a little reminder that slowing down is a good thing, this is your place.

Thank you for giving me the best nail salon experience I’ve ever had. I’ll definitely be back!

reviewList.text:
If there were a 0-star rating option, I would give it immediately… I had been to this salon once before and returned for a simple gel polish and nail extensions! The issue I'm talking about here isn't about whether it's good or bad, but the ATTITUDE OF THE STAFF AND THE OWNER! This is a newly opened nail salon in Thanh Khe… The first time I went, I got a plain gel polish on my natural nails, but after 7 days, the polish chipped and the tips were peeling off, even though I don't do much housework. At other places I've been to, even if the polish chipped, it would take at least two weeks to fix it! But at this salon, it chipped after only 7 days! I messaged the salon to ask them to improve their technique, and they offered a warranty and a 10% discount on my next visit… I don't have time to go through the trouble of getting two sets of nails done a week like that! I told them I'd reschedule for another time! The second time I went, I messaged the salon beforehand to book an appointment. They scheduled me for 6:15-6:30, and when I arrived at 6:00, someone was waiting for me. My sister had also had her hair washed there! It was great! But it wasn't like that for me... At 6:45, I still hadn't been served. I was fine with waiting and understanding, but when it came to filing the shape, even someone unfamiliar with the profession could see that it wasn't even. The middle finger was noticeably shorter than all the other nails, and it was particularly crooked!!! I told the staff member who was doing it to me, and she got annoyed and said, "I don't see anything short, ma'am, I see it's even." I pointed out that she needed to refile and redo it because a beautiful set of nails depends on the shape... She blamed my large, rough, and unattractive nails, saying, "What?!" If it were beautiful, I wouldn't have done it; it would have been beautiful as it was. I told the staff member, "Your hands clearly have a large, prominent crease, but even with your technicians, how can you make them look harmonious and beautiful for the client?" The staff member replied, "I'M NOT A DOCTOR, SIR!! HOW CAN I MAKE YOUR HANDS BEAUTIFUL?" Oh my god, how shameless! I've worked at many salons and have never received such an attitude, action, or words towards a customer! When the staff member called the owner, the owner couldn't resolve anything and acted exactly like the staff member! OMG! As the owner, I should at least have a polite and respectful attitude towards customers, but instead, they were sullen and rude!

I'm not picky; I don't care if the nail work is good or bad, or if the skills aren't perfect. But the service and attitude were TERRIBLE. If they had been cheerful, friendly, and apologized, I would have been happy to continue working on it, not to get so angry that I had to remove everything and leave! It was a huge waste of my time! I wasted two and a half hours only to have my hands look worse than before! It was such a waste of time and such a terrible experience! With this kind of business practice, customers will leave sooner or later! I messaged the owner, but they remained silent! It's outrageous! Everyone should consider avoiding this nail salon and not let it be like what happened to me!!
reviewList.author: Bo Dung

reviewList.text: My usual salon was closed for maternity leave, so I happened to get my hair washed at this one. It's a newly opened salon, quite empty, the staff are young, and the space is spacious, airy, and clean, so I've come back many times to support them and hope they'll have more customers in the future. There are two staff members; one is quite thorough with the shampoo and massage, while the other is a bit more perfunctory. The first time I got my nails done here, I found the method quite unusual, but the nails were durable and the staff were careful and meticulous, so I trusted them and got my box nails done. They were quite quick to do my nails and didn't ask any questions, which made me a little worried, but since it was my first time getting my nails done, I went along with it. However, my easygoing attitude backfired on their carelessness and lack of respect. When they attached the box nails to my first finger, they didn't pay attention, allowing air bubbles to get inside, making them visibly inflated (the gel nails are transparent, so you can see the air bubbles underneath). I immediately told them, "Please be careful because with air bubbles inside, the nails could easily fall off." But after all ten nails were done, 4 or 5 of them had the same air bubbles 🥲. You also measured the size incorrectly, making the nails smaller than my natural nails. If you had noticed the mistake, you should have redone those nails or let me know if you wanted them adjusted or if a slightly smaller size would have been acceptable. But you didn't do that. Even when I complained about it, I didn't receive any apology; you just stayed silent and simply didn't care. Normally, I get a set of nails done every 3-4 weeks, so a little imperfection is fine, but these are New Year's nails, how can you expect me to wear them like this at the beginning of the new year? (The salon wasn't busy at all, so you can't say it was because it was too busy that you did a sloppy job. Even if it were busy, an apology wouldn't take more than 10 seconds). Since it's close to Tet (Vietnamese New Year), the salon has slightly increased prices. I suggest you inform customers beforehand, for example, about a 10% surcharge during Tet or something similar, before they book or for regular customers. But the extra charge was negligible, so it was still acceptable. The staff were rather introverted; they didn't even greet customers, thank them, or say "I've received your transfer." They ignored customers as they left, sitting on their phones without even glancing at them or saying "come visit us next time," or "if you need your nails removed, come over and we'll help you," etc. Every time I finished a service, I felt like I had suddenly disappeared. Each regular customer is a potential gold mine; loyal customers who want to return are essential for long-term business. Normally, a customer gets 10-15 sets of nails done per year and hair washes 1-3 times a week. With that kind of behavior, how can you expect customers to come back? You should try working at other busy salons to see how their staff provide service. Since the salon is new, I hope you improve your service and attract more customers, retaining them.

Bumped into this place while i was looking for a money exchange shop and couldn't find any since my phone didn't have internet connection. I randomly asked one of the staff to point me to the nearest money exchange and even helped me get quick access to internet for proper google maps directions.

The following day, I went back to the store to avail one of their services as a way to thank them for the kindness they've shown the previous day. I've been walking on an average of 15k steps/day while exploring Da Nang and just realized maybe it's finally time to get a foot scrub and foot massage for the first time in my life (since i've also noticed that it is in almost every street near my hotel).

Surprisingly the foot scrub did not hurt at all. It kinda looked gross to see all the dry skins be flying all over the towel which made me feel bad for the staff doing it since it's my first time experiencing this haha. I even had to type in Google Translate how sorry i was. Out of embarrassment, i just gave a slightly higher tip to the staff. Even now that i left Da Nang my foot is still smooth and still feels unusual for a first timer.

I loved the friendliness of the staffs that i had to go back the following day and avail of their foot massage before i leave the country. This time the staff who accommodated me really took her time with the foot massage which i genuinely liked. The pressure was not that hard as much as i wanted it to be but it's decent to feel relaxed especially with the hot stone. (I also just didn't know how to properly communicate that i wanted stronger pressure haha).

Overall, it was nothing fancy or high-end, but it was definitely a great and memorable experience for me as a first timer and will definitely be back if I get a chance to visit Da Nang again in the future.

I highly recommend this nail salon! It is clean, beautiful with good music and the nail artists are so friendly and nice.

I love their designs and the prices are so good. You’d pay anything between 120-160k for a hand drawn design.
